..
Issued at 300 PM EDT Wed Sep 9 2026

Currently-Tonight... KMLB radar imagery shows scattered generally 
west-northwest moving showers and lightning storms across east 
central Florida (mainly along and south of I-4). GOES-19 satellite 
imagery and local observations indicate partly to mostly cloudy 
skies across east central Florida. Temperatures are currently in the 
mid 80s to low 90s, heat index values are between 100F-108F degrees, 
and dew points are between the mid 70s to around 80F degrees. 
Analysis charts show a stationary boundary over east central Florida 
with higher moisture to the south of the boundary with PWATs up to 
2.2." Additionally, the 15Z XMR sounding shows MLCAPE at 2,524
J/kg, PWAT at 2.28", MidRH at 85%, LowRH 87%, relatively warm 500mb
temperatures at -3.6C, and 0-6km shear at 23kts with an MDP value
of 1.1.

Coverage of showers and lightning storms are forecast to increase in 
coverage late this afternoon and evening as collisions occur between 
easterly flow, the west coast sea breeze over the western interior 
of central Florida, and outflow from previous storms. Rain chances 
are forecast to gradually diminish around 8PM. Isolated onshore 
moving showers/lightning storms are forecast tonight and into the 
overnight. Conditions are favorable for a strong storm capable of
frequent lightning, wind gusts up to 40-50mph, and heavy rainfall
(up to 1-3" in 60 minutes). Near to above normal (~1-4F+ degrees)
low temperatures in the mid 70s to around 80 degrees are 
forecast.

Thursday-Friday... The weather pattern is expected to transition 
to a more typical sea breeze driven pattern Thursday into Friday 
as the Bermuda high builds west over the western Atlantic waters 
and the stationary boundary "washes out" over east central 
Florida. South-southeast winds at 5-10mph on Thursday will veer 
offshore Thursday night before backing onshore into Friday 
afternoon as the east coast sea breeze pushes inland. Scattered to
numerous showers (40-70% chance) and lightning storms are forecast
to develop each afternoon with the greatest coverage along and
near I-4 where the greatest surface convergence is forecast.
Guidance shows a typical environment for sea breeze driven 
showers and lightning storms with high instability, low shear, and
plentiful moisture. However, guidance shows 500mb PVA pivoting 
across east central Florida on Friday which suggests that there is
greater potential for strong storms on Friday than what we have 
seen in more recent days. The primary hazards with a strong storm 
or two on Thursday and a couple to a few strong storms on Friday 
are frequent (frequent to excessive lightning on Friday), wind 
gusts up to 40-50mph (<5% chance of wind gusts up to 60mph on 
Friday), and heavy rainfall (up to 1-3" in 60 minutes). Afternoon 
highs in the upper 80s to low 90s with heat index values up to 
102F-107F are forecast. Above normal lows (~1-4+ degrees) in the 
low to upper 70s are forecast. There is a Moderate HeatRisk with 
pockets of Major HeatRisk on Thursday and Friday. A Moderate 
HeatRisk affects those sensitive to heat and a Major HeatRisk 
affects anyone without adequate cooling and hydration. 

Saturday-Tuesday... The active weather pattern is expected to
continue over the weekend and into next week. The western fringe 
of the Bermuda high is forecast to become established over the 
local Atlantic waters, as well as high pressure over the eastern
Gulf on Monday. Scattered to numerous/widespread showers (between
50-80% chance) and lightning storms are forecast to develop each 
day in the afternoon and evening before rain chances diminish into
the late evening, as well as overnight hours. High instability 
with weak shear and sufficient moisture is forecast which is 
conducive for isolated to scattered strong storms capable of 
frequent lightning, strong wind gusts, and heavy rainfall. There
is a up to 20-70% chance of a Major HeatRisk for areas of east 
central Florida Saturday to Monday with lower chances on Tuesday 
(up to 20-50% chance).
